metaDescription: Margaux tomato is a tomato variety. About 63 days to harvest, 11.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Margaux is a registered tomato variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2016 as NSIC 2016 Tm 17. It takes about 63 days from transplanting to the first harvest, with 11.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Yield:** 11.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Margaux tomato takes about 63 days from transplanting to the first harvest. That is 7.6 days faster than the average of the 20 tomato varieties with a day count, 70.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 11.2 t/ha trails the average of its group, 20.91. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.text: It was weak against bacterial wilt, so scout for it from the early weeks. Read up on [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt).

The pests and diseases that hit tomato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Margaux tomato

It is recommended for the dry season. Bacterial wilt kills more lowland tomato than any other disease, so in the wet season pick a variety rated resistant to it. Choose a firm, oblong fruit if you sell to a far market, and a round, juicy one for fresh sale nearby. Heat tolerant hybrids set fruit in the hot months, when open pollinated tomatoes often drop their flowers. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 63 days from transplanting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 11.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Margaux?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
